manifest.name: Caregiving Binder

tools.description: Mark a medication stopped (with why, when known).

tools.name: log_appointment
tools.description: Record an appointment (what and when, ISO).

tools.name: care_status
tools.description: Active meds, upcoming appointments, journal count.

tools.name: visit_prep
tools.description: The one-page brief for the next doctor visit: meds + what happened since the last one.

manifest.name: Checkers
manifest.description: Play checkers against a gezel opponent on a live board. You move on the board; the Damspeler ("checkers player") sees the position, plays back, and keeps the table talk going.

personality.title: Table-talk style
personality.description: How your opponent talks between moves.

playStyle.title: How should the Damspeler play?
playStyle.description: An opponent keeps their strategy to themselves; an instructor offers light teaching notes.

tools.name: get_board
tools.description: See the authoritative structured checkers position, whose turn it is, capture availability, and every legal move. A legacy ASCII board is included for human readability.

tools.name: make_move
tools.description: Play your (black's) move. Pass the from/to squares of a legal move; include a short moveThought to show on the board.

to.description: Destination square (a jump's final landing square).

moveThought.description: A short line of table talk (max 140 chars).

tools.name: user_move
tools.description: The user's move, played from the board page.

reaction.prompt:
Your opponent played {{output.lastMove}}. The game engine returned this authoritative state:
```json
{{output.modelState}}
```
Every `legalMoves` entry is legal. Its `type` and `captures` fields explicitly say whether it is a jump. Do not redraw the position as a grid, re-derive legality, recalculate capture availability, recount pieces, or question the stated orientation. Spend any thinking only on which listed move is strongest.
Style: {{playStyle}}. In Opponent style, do not volunteer advice or reveal the user's available moves, captures, threats, or tactics; comment only about your own move or the atmosphere. In Instructor style, offer at most one brief teaching observation without choosing the user's move. Answer strategy questions when asked.
Act on the state above. If the game is over, do not move — one gracious line and offer new_game. Otherwise it is your turn: choose one listed move and call make_move with its `from` and `to` strings, including a short {{personality}} moveThought that follows the selected style. If make_move rejects it, choose one move from the legal list in the error and try again. After moving, reply with ONE short line of table talk that follows the selected style.

tools.name: new_game
tools.description: Reset the board to the opening position (user moves first).

forceCaptures.description: Whether captures are required when available. Defaults to true.

manifest.name: Chess
manifest.description: Play a complete game of chess against a gezel opponent on a live board. You move white; the Schaakspeler sees the exact position, replies with a legal move, and shares the table without spoiling your plans.

personality.title: Table-talk style
personality.description: How your opponent talks between moves.

playStyle.title: How should the Schaakspeler play?
playStyle.description: An opponent keeps their strategy to themselves; an instructor offers light teaching notes.

tools.name: get_board
tools.description: See the authoritative chess position, whose turn it is, and every legal move.

tools.name: make_move
tools.description: Play your black move. Pass from/to; for promotion optionally choose 'q', 'r', 'b', or 'n'. Include a short moveThought for the board.

moveThought.description: A short line of table talk (max 140 chars).

tools.name: user_move
tools.description: The user's white move, played from the chess board.

reaction.prompt:
Your opponent played {{output.lastMove}}. Status: {{output.status}}. Board now:
{{output.board}}
The board and Legal moves line come directly from the chess engine and are always correct. Do not re-derive the position, dispute a listed move, or invent a move outside that list. Spend your thought on choosing among the listed legal moves.
Style: {{playStyle}}. In Opponent style, do not volunteer advice or reveal the user’s available moves, threats, tactics, or your plan; comment only about your own move or the atmosphere. In Instructor style, offer at most one brief teaching observation without choosing the user’s move. Answer strategy questions when asked.
Act on this latest position. If the game is over, do not move — give one gracious line and offer a new game. Otherwise choose a strong legal move and play it with make_move, including a short {{personality}} moveThought that follows the selected style. If make_move rejects it, choose one move verbatim from the legal list in the error and retry. After moving, reply with ONE short line of table talk.

tools.name: new_game
tools.description: Reset the chess board to the standard opening position.

manifest.name: Go
manifest.description: Play Go against a gezel opponent on a live 9×9, 13×13, or 19×19 board. Place black stones; the Go-speler reads the exact position, replies in white, and keeps the conversation calm and sporting.

personality.title: Table-talk style
personality.description: How your opponent talks between moves.

playStyle.title: How should the Go-speler play?
playStyle.description: An opponent keeps their strategy to themselves; an instructor offers light teaching notes.

tools.name: get_board
tools.description: See the authoritative Go position, board size, captures, whose turn it is, and every legal move.

tools.name: make_move
tools.description: Play your white move. Pass a coordinate such as 'D4', or 'pass', plus optional moveThought.

move.description: A legal coordinate such as 'D4', or 'pass'.

moveThought.description: A short line of table talk (max 140 chars).

tools.name: user_move
tools.description: The user's black move or pass, played from the Go board.

reaction.prompt:
Your opponent played {{output.lastMove}}. Status: {{output.status}}. Board now:
{{output.board}}
The board and Legal moves line come directly from the Go engine and are always correct. Do not re-derive captures, liberties, ko, scoring, or legality, and do not invent a coordinate outside the legal list. Spend your thought on choosing among the listed moves.
Style: {{playStyle}}. In Opponent style, do not volunteer advice or reveal the user’s available moves, weak groups, threats, or your plan; comment only about your own move or the atmosphere. In Instructor style, offer at most one brief teaching observation without choosing the user’s move. Answer strategy questions when asked.
Act on this latest position. If the game is over, do not move — give one gracious line about the result and offer a new game. Otherwise choose a strong legal move (or pass when strategically sound) and play it with make_move, including a short {{personality}} moveThought. If make_move rejects it, choose one move verbatim from the legal list in the error and retry. After moving, reply with ONE short line of table talk.

tools.name: new_game
tools.description: Reset the Go board. Choose 9, 13, or 19 lines and optional komi; defaults to 9×9 with 6.5 komi.

manifest.description: A visual feed with a working rhythm — your Omroeper runs the posting pipeline, an image maker turns notions into pictures in the feed's own style, and a live gallery shows every post from first idea to published.

brand.title: Who does this feed speak for?
brand.description: The name, brand, or studio this feed speaks for.

instagramHandle.title: Instagram handle
instagramHandle.description: Instagram handle (e.g. @studio). Leave empty if unused.

visualStyle.title: Visual style
visualStyle.description: One sentence on how the feed should look — seeded into style-guide.md.
visualStyle.default: Natural light, honest color, one subject per image.

voice.title: Tone of voice
voice.description: One sentence on tone of voice for captions.
voice.default: Warm, plain, and human — never corporate.

cadence.title: Posting cadence
cadence.description: Target posting cadence (e.g. 4 images a week).

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description: See the whole post pipeline: every post with its status, platforms, and dates. Optionally filter by status or platform.

status.description: Only posts currently in this status.

platform.description: Only posts targeting this platform, e.g. 'bluesky'.

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: Read one post in full: frontmatter, body, each platform variant with its character count (and permalink once live), and media files.

id.description: Post id — its folder name under posts/, e.g. '2026-08-12-launch-teaser'.

tools.name: create_post
tools.description: Commit the staged posts/_drafting/ folder as a real post. Stage post.md (frontmatter + body), variants/, and media/ there first; the post folder is named from the created date and slug.

status.description: Initial status for the new post. Defaults to approved.

tools.name: update_post
tools.description: Patch a post's frontmatter (fields object; null clears a key) and/or move it one pipeline stage. Stages run idea, draft, in-review, approved, scheduled, published — archived from anywhere.

status.description: Target status (one stage at a time).

tools.name: record_publication
tools.description: The moment a variant goes live, stamp it with its permalink and platform post id. The post flips to published once every target platform is stamped (or markPublished is passed).

platform.description: The platform that went live, e.g. 'bluesky'.

permalink.description: Public URL of the live post.

postId.description: The platform's own id for the live post.

corpusRef.description: Connector corpus record reference, when one exists.

publishedAt.description: ISO timestamp it went live (defaults to now).

markPublished.description: Force the post to published even with unstamped platforms.

tools.name: page_set_status
tools.description: Page-only: move a post between pipeline columns on the gallery.

status.description: The column the post was moved to.

reaction.prompt: [Feed gallery]: The user moved post {{output.id}} to '{{output.status}}' on the gallery. Reply with ONE short line acknowledging the move. If it landed in 'draft', offer to run the draft-social-post craftbook on it. Do not restate the pipeline.

tools.name: page_get_post
tools.description: Page-only: the detail drawer's read of one post with variants and media.

manifest.notes: posts/index.json is seeded at its subpath (applyProjectType preserves seed subpaths and creates parents) and is ALSO regenerated by posts-store on every mutation, so the gallery tolerates a missing or stale index. Posts live one folder per post under posts/ (post.md + variants/ + media/), staged in posts/_drafting/ until create_post commits them. page_set_status and page_get_post are the page-only twins of update_post/get_post — pages.tools names are removed from the model surface, so the model keeps its own read tools.
